[Films](Film "Film") generate income from several revenue streams, including [theatrical exhibition](Movie_theater "Movie theater"), [home video](Home_video "Home video"), [television broadcast rights](Broadcasting_rights "Broadcasting rights"), and [merchandising](Merchandising "Merchandising"). However, theatrical [box-office](Box_office "Box office") earnings are the primary metric for trade publications in assessing the success of a film, mostly because of the availability of the data compared to sales figures for home video and broadcast rights, but also because of historical practice. Included on the list are charts of the top box-office earners (ranked by both the [nominal and real value](Real_versus_nominal_value_(economics) "Real versus nominal value (economics)") of their revenue), a chart of high-grossing films by calendar year, a timeline showing the transition of the highest-grossing film record, and a chart of the highest-grossing film franchises and series. All charts are ranked by international theatrical box-office performance where possible, excluding income derived from home video, broadcasting rights, and merchandise.

Traditionally, [war films](War_film "War film"), [musicals](Musical_film "Musical film"), and [historical dramas](List_of_historical_drama_films "List of historical drama films") have been the most popular genres, but [franchise films](Media_franchise "Media franchise") have been among the best performers of the 21st century. There is strong interest in the [superhero genre](Superhero_film "Superhero film"), with ten films in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") featuring among the nominal top-earners. The most successful superhero film, *[Avengers: Endgame](Avengers%3A_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")*, is also the second-highest-grossing film on the nominal earnings chart, and there are four films in total based on the *[Avengers](Avengers_(comics) "Avengers (comics)")* comic books charting in the top twenty. Other [Marvel Comics adaptations](List_of_films_based_on_Marvel_Comics "List of films based on Marvel Comics") have also had success with the *[Spider-Man](Spider-Man_in_film "Spider-Man in film")* and *[X-Men](X-Men_(film_series) "X-Men (film series)")* properties, while films based on *[Batman](Batman_in_film "Batman in film")* and *[Superman](Superman_in_film "Superman in film")* from [DC Comics](DC_Comics "DC Comics") have generally performed well. *[Star Wars](Star_Wars "Star Wars")* is also represented in the nominal earnings chart with five films, while the *[Jurassic Park](Jurassic_Park "Jurassic Park")* franchise features prominently. Although the nominal earnings chart is dominated by films adapted from pre-existing properties and sequels, it is headed by *[Avatar](Avatar_(2009_film) "Avatar (2009 film)")*, which is an original work. Animated family films have performed consistently well, with [Disney films](List_of_Disney_theatrical_animated_features "List of Disney theatrical animated features") enjoying lucrative re-releases prior to the home-video era. Disney also enjoyed later success with films such as *[Frozen](Frozen_(2013_film) "Frozen (2013 film)")* and *[Frozen II](Frozen_II "Frozen II")*, *<Zootopia>*, and *[The Lion King](The_Lion_King "The Lion King")* (with [its computer-animated remake](The_Lion_King_(2019_film) "The Lion King (2019 film)") as the [highest-grossing animated film](List_of_highest-grossing_animated_films "List of highest-grossing animated films")), as well as its [Pixar](List_of_Pixar_films "List of Pixar films") brand, of which *[Incredibles 2](Incredibles_2 "Incredibles 2")*, *[Toy Story 3](Toy_Story_3 "Toy Story 3")* and *[4](Toy_Story_4 "Toy Story 4")*, and *[Finding Dory](Finding_Dory "Finding Dory")* have been the best performers. Beyond Disney and Pixar animation, the *[Despicable Me](Despicable_Me "Despicable Me")*, *[Shrek](Shrek_(franchise) "Shrek (franchise)")*, and *[Ice Age](Ice_Age_(franchise) "Ice Age (franchise)")* series have met with the most success.

While [inflation](Inflation "Inflation") has eroded the achievements of most films from the 1950s, 1960s, and 1970s, there are franchises originating from that period that are still active. Besides the *Star Wars* and *Superman* franchises, *[James Bond](James_Bond_in_film "James Bond in film")* and *[Godzilla](Godzilla_(franchise) "Godzilla (franchise)")* films are still being released periodically; all four are among the highest-grossing franchises. Some of the older films that held the record of highest-grossing film still have respectable grosses by today's standards, but no longer compete numerically against today's top-earners in an era of much higher individual ticket prices. When those prices are adjusted for inflation, however, then *[Gone with the Wind](Gone_with_the_Wind_(film) "Gone with the Wind (film)")*—which was the highest-grossing film outright for twenty-five years—is still the highest-grossing film of all time. All grosses on the list are expressed in [U.S. dollars](United_States_dollar "United States dollar") at their nominal value, except where stated otherwise.

## Highest-grossing films

With a worldwide box-office gross of over $2.9 billion, *Avatar* is proclaimed to be the "highest-grossing" film, but such claims usually refer to [theatrical](Movie_theatre "Movie theatre") revenues only and do not take into account [home video](Home_video "Home video") and [television](Television "Television") income, which can form a significant portion of a film's earnings. Once revenue from home entertainment is factored in, it is not immediately clear which film is the most successful. *[Titanic](Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* earned $1.2 billion from [video](Video "Video") and [DVD](DVD-Video "DVD-Video") sales and rentals,[[1]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) in addition to the $2.2 billion it grossed in theatres. While complete sales data are not available for *Avatar*, it earned $345 million from the sale of sixteen million DVD and <Blu-ray> units in North America,[[2]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-2) and ultimately sold a total of thirty million DVD and Blu-ray units worldwide.[[3]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-3) After home video income is accounted for, both films have earned over $3 billion each. Television [broadcast](Broadcasting "Broadcasting") rights will also substantially add to a film's earnings, with a film often earning the equivalent of as much as 20–25% of its theatrical box office for two television runs, on top of [pay-per-view](Pay-per-view "Pay-per-view") revenues;[[4]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-4) *Titanic* earned a further $55 million from the <NBC> and <HBO> broadcast rights,[[1]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) equating to about 9% of its North American gross.

When a film is highly exploitable as a commercial property, its ancillary revenues can dwarf its income from direct film sales.[[5]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-5) *The Lion King* (1994) earned over $2 billion in box-office and home video sales,[[1]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) but this pales in comparison to the $8 billion earned at box offices around the world by [the stage adaptation](The_Lion_King_(musical) "The Lion King (musical)").[[6]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-6) <Merchandising> can be extremely lucrative too: *The Lion King* also sold $3 billion of merchandise,[[7]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-7) while Pixar's *[Cars](Cars_(film) "Cars (film)")*—which earned $462 million in theatrical revenues and was only a modest hit by comparison to other [Pixar films](List_of_Pixar_films "List of Pixar films")[[8]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-8)—generated global merchandise sales of over $8 billion in the five years after its 2006 release.[[9]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-9)[[10]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-10) Pixar had another huge hit with *Toy Story 3*, which generated almost $10 billion in merchandise retail sales in addition to the $1 billion it earned at the box office.[[11]](List_of_highest-grossing_films#cite_note-11)

On this chart, films are ranked by the revenues from theatrical exhibition at their nominal value, along with the highest positions they attained. Six films in total have grossed in excess of $2 billion worldwide, with *Avatar* ranked in the top position. All of the films have had a theatrical run (including re-releases) in the 21st century, and films that have not played during this period do not appear on the chart because of ticket-price inflation, population size and ticket purchasing trends not being considered.

Based on the Wikipedia article "List of highest-grossing films," here are the worldwide gross earnings (in U.S. dollars) of the all-time top five highest-grossing movies:

| Rank | Title | Year | Worldwide Gross Earnings |

- The **Marvel Cinematic Universe** is well-represented with *Avengers: Endgame* at #2
- All of these films achieved their massive success in the 21st century, benefiting from global theatrical distribution and higher ticket prices
